source.title: Talking Heads: Understanding Inter-layer Communication in Transformer Language Models
source.authors: Jack Merullo; Carsten Eickhoff; Ellie Pavlick

record.file_problem: The full paper is present, but some figure text and OCR are garbled or flattened.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests whether selected low-rank components in the IOI inhibition–mover subcircuit affect inhibition and name selection, using component edits and activation interventions rather than reproducing the original full-circuit analysis.
record.gate_note: The results concern selected inhibition, duplicate-token, mover, and related components; they do not evaluate the full 26-head, 7-class circuit or all of its stated criteria. Cited results from Wang et al. are not recorded as findings of this study. Several figure-only intervention curves are described qualitatively in the text.
record.test_reason: Uses SVD weight decomposition, component removal, activation steering and subspace patching to test the roles of IOI-circuit heads in GPT-2 small. These are the duplicate-token head 3.0, S-inhibition heads 7.3/7.9/8.6/8.10 and name mover 9.9. It also checks whether a similar inhibition–mover channel exists in Pythia-160m and is reused in a Laundry List task. Appendix H recovers IOI-circuit heads from weights alone, which bears on V4.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but the 'partial mechanism' framing is the record's, not the authors'. The authors conclude that heads communicate through very low-rank subspaces identifiable from SVD-decomposed weights, and that these channels are causally important and content-independent. A 3D inhibition subspace positionally indexes list items, which explains order sensitivity and capacity failures on longer lists. Interventions on it raise Laundry List accuracy by over 20%, and a similar channel exists in Pythia-160m.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SVD-decomposed weight components, component removal/editing, and activation interventions or subspace patching to study selected IOI subcircuit roles; it does not reproduce the original full-circuit discovery and evaluation recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The effect depends on which inhibition component is edited: 7.3 has little effect, while other single-component removals reduce inhibition by 7-14%. A single component cannot index all objects in multi-object prompts; the three-dimensional inhibition subspace shows capacity limits as list length grows.

fits_no_version.finding: Weight-based search finds heads 6.1, 6.2, 6.7 and 8.3 composing strongly with mover 9.9, which were not in the original circuit. 8.3 modulates inhibition scores, but removing 8.3.0 reduces inhibition by less than .01. 8.3 attends to plausible continuations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Additional heads outside the published IOI circuit feed the name mover's queries.

fits_no_version.finding: Inhibition heads are active on comma-separated lists in OpenWebText, attending to earlier list items (Appendix F, qualitative).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: IOI S-inhibition heads serve a general repetition-avoidance and list-indexing role in open text.

record.problems: Tests selected subcircuit components rather than the full claimed circuit; some intervention results are figure-only; the cited patching comparison is to a result from another study; the Pythia evidence is limited to one model size and does not establish cross-model circuit identity.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows left out. Larger-model Laundry List accuracy curves (Appendix A, Figure 6) are not rows for these versions because they do not intervene on or measure the IOI circuit or its components.

untested.parts: The full 26-head, 7-class circuit; the faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria; negative and backup name movers; previous-token and induction heads in their IOI role. Only one name mover (9.9) is examined.
Entire version: there is no ablation of the name movers and no test for backup takeover.
Other GPT-2 or Pythia sizes; whether the full head-class structure reappears in Pythia; whether the circuit is present at each training checkpoint (only figure-level data).
Other ablation types and metrics; any quantitative overlap between the weight-derived circuit and the original circuit.
Ablation type and prompt distribution are not varied for the full circuit.
Other IOI templates, more names in IOI prompts, and whether other formats use different components.

missing.what: Decomposed composition scores recover the IOI-circuit heads from weights without running the model (qualitative).
Copying test: 9.9 scores 100%, while the inhibition heads and 8.3 score 0%.
Inhibition heads are highly active on Laundry List, attending to and inhibiting repeated objects.
Original inhibition score and 6.6.2 separability across Pythia training checkpoints (figure only).
Control heads (8.0.0, 8.3.0, random) do not reproduce the positional control.

record.verdict_notes: R6 and R7 baselines are cited from Makelov et al. R16 and R17 are editing interventions, not measurements of the circuit arising during training. Laundry List rows were moved from V6 to V3 (task reuse). The V4 support is qualitative and comes from the appendix only.

versions.untested_parts: Tests selected components and their effects on inhibition/name selection, not the complete 26-head, 7-class circuit or its faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria.
No ablation of main name-mover heads to test whether backup heads take over.

Tests selected IOI-related components in Pythia-160m, including training-checkpoint analyses; does not establish that the same circuit carries IOI across other sizes or models, or that these components are reused for other tasks.
Does not compare circuit-finding methods, ablation types, or metrics for recovery of the same circuit.
Provides some evidence of incomplete effects and compares output-related measures, but does not systematically vary ablation type, metric, or prompt distribution to establish their sensitivity.

Tests IOI name orders and an inhibition-channel intervention on multi-object Laundry List prompts; does not systematically compare circuit components across prompt templates or establish generalization to all prompt variants.

rows.subject: GPT2-Small
rows.operation_detail: Zeroed the single highest-composition component in an inhibition head, one head at a time.
rows.measure: Inhibition score (mover-head attention to IO minus attention to S1)
rows.value: Removing the component reduced the inhibition score by 7-14% in general.
rows.note: The reported range is across single-component edits; the paper notes an exception for 7.3, recorded separately in R2.
rows.check: Removing one rank-1 component from one S-inhibition head cuts inhibition by 7-14%, which confirms that head's role. This does not measure how sensitive the evaluation is, so the V5 link is dropped. Baseline (full-model inhibition about 0.7, Fig. 2) is not recorded.

rows.subject: GPT2-Small
rows.operation_detail: Removed the speculated communication component from head 7.3.
rows.value: Changing 7.3 does not have a strong effect on its own.
rows.note: The paper explicitly describes this as an exception to the general 7-14% decrease.
rows.check: The V5 link is dropped. The row bears on whether head 7.3, one of the original S-inhibition heads, contributes through its top component.

rows.subject: GPT2-Small
rows.operation_detail: Overwrote an attention-head output with a scaled 8.10.1 component vector, bypassing that head's attention pattern.
rows.note: The text says scaling the component changes which name the mover attends to; downscaling increases inhibition when S1 is first and decreases it when IO is first. The reciprocal pattern occurs when upscaling.
rows.check: The V6 link holds only for name order (IO-first vs S1-first), not for templates or more names. Figure only.

rows.subject: GPT2-Small
rows.operation_detail: Overwrote an attention-head output with a scaled 8.10.1 component vector, bypassing that head's attention pattern.
rows.note: The text describes the positional effect and its opposite direction from the IO-first condition.
rows.check: Same as R3: the V6 link covers name order only. Figure only.

rows.subject: GPT2-Small
rows.operation_detail: Kept only the top composing component in each inhibition head and removed other components.
rows.note: The paper describes this as retaining close to half of the average inhibition score.
rows.check: The V5 link is dropped. Keeping only the top components retains about 0.3 of 0.7 inhibition, so the signal is spread across more than one component per head.

rows.subject: GPT2-Small
rows.operation_detail: Kept only the zeroth singular-value component of each inhibition head.
rows.note: The result is a small but nonzero inhibition score compared with the full model.
rows.check: This is a control condition: keeping the zeroth, non-communication components gives 0.04. It shows that component selection matters, not how well the circuit or version holds.

rows.subject: GPT2-Small
rows.operation_detail: Set the model's inhibition components to a selected point in the three-dimensional inhibition space, chosen based on the correct answer index.
rows.note: The task requires retrieving the missing item from a list of objects.
rows.check: This is a different task (Laundry List), not an IOI prompt variant. It bears on V3 (reuse of IOI components for other tasks), not V6. The value comes from an intervention chosen using the correct answer index.

rows.subject: GPT2-Small
rows.operation_detail: Set the model's inhibition components to a selected point in the three-dimensional inhibition space, chosen based on the correct answer index.
rows.baseline: not stated; authors compare the result to the unmodified model's accuracy at 4 objects
rows.note: The authors describe this as roughly the unmodified model's 4-object accuracy, and say the channel's representational capacity limits further gains as list length grows.
rows.check: Relinked from V6 to V3 because it is task reuse. No 8-object unmodified baseline is stated; the text compares only to the 4-object level.

rows.subject: GPT2-Small
rows.operation_detail: Scaled a single inhibition component on a multi-object Laundry List task.
rows.value: The mover tends to attend to either the first or last object, grouping the remaining objects together.
rows.note: The authors state that one component at a time is insufficient to direct attention across all the objects.
rows.check: Relinked from V6 to V3. It describes the limited expressivity of a single component on another task.

rows.subject: Pythia-160m
rows.operation_detail: Applied path patching on IOI to examine whether the model implements mover and inhibition heads.
rows.measure: Evidence for an inhibition-head to mover-head interaction
rows.value: Evidence for inhibition head 6.6 communicating with mover head 9.5.
rows.note: The paper also reports that inhibition component 6.6.2 dominates the interaction and that induction head 4.11 strongly value-composes with it; it does not provide a numeric path-patching effect here.
rows.check: Only one inhibition head (6.6) and one mover (9.5) are reported in Pythia, versus four S-inhibition heads in GPT-2. No numeric path-patching effect is given.

source_check.correct: State: observed for the identified inhibition-head 6.6 to mover-head 9.5 interaction. The remaining head classes are untested here; their incomplete mapping does not establish weaker or incomplete operation.
source_check.problem: The partial state treats limited circuit coverage as evidence of an incomplete effect.

rows.subject: Pythia-160m

rows.note: The text states that adding the component improves the ability to use inhibition in earlier checkpoints.

relationships.reason: Top-component removal lowers mover inhibition (R1). Scaling the 8.10.1 and 3.0 channels controls which name 9.9 avoids (R3-R5). Inhibition-subspace patching gives FLDD 97.5% (R6).
